description: The record kind is added when the ids match across kinds; an uncontested title shows nothing. Verified by property including chip minimality. Amended 2026-08-10: enforcement is now genuinely per page - one renderer sees every titled link a page renders, including decision titles, citations, and classification rows, so cross-section collisions get chips.
statement: Two links sharing a title but meaning different records each show the shortest ending of their id that tells them apart, never fewer than eight characters

description: Identical content passes; records behind no assertion change freely. Two readings of cited: a contribution through the claim ids an assertion supports, a synthesis packet by the id it names - both are uses of one shared core, so the freeze cannot drift between kinds. Import hand-derives the same freeze and drifted on deletion (tracked in beads).
statement: A record cited by an assertion cannot be replaced with different content

description: The sibling of rule_asserted_evidence_immutable: import stands a whole scope in place of the stored one, so it is the only path that can drop a record; a dropped cited contribution and a dropped asserted synthesis packet now error identically. Citedness is read with the store's own predicates, so the freeze and the deletion rule ask the same question.
statement: A record cited by an assertion cannot be deleted

description: Resolved and archived threads never win, and a record with no active thread has no canonical thread. Verified by property over generated thread lists with deliberate ties. The live path in thread_writers also archives the losing active siblings; that archiving is now rule_thread_siblings_archived, marked and property-verified.
statement: choose_canonical_active_thread picks the oldest active thread as canonical, breaking created_at ties by lower id

description: The dual of rule_claim_eligibility: entry and exit guard the same set of statuses, proven by an exhaustion test asserting claim_survives equals no-blocking-status over all six ShapingStatus values. Written independently of the eligibility predicate so the duality proof is not vacuous.
statement: A claim does not survive its record leaving the claimable state: closing a topic, answering a question, or blocking it on a human clears the claim

description: One decision over both status enums; the refusal names the state with the word the record stores. Proven exhaustively over all six statuses. The dual is rule_claim_cleared_on_exit, extracted 2026-08-10 with an exhaustion proof that entry and exit agree exactly. Review note 2026-08-10: the eligibility check now runs before proposal surfacing, so a closed topic in a scope with a corrupt proposal shard reports the closure rather than the parse error - a deliberate error-order change.
statement: Shaping work may be claimed only while its record is open for work: a closed topic, or an answered or human-blocked question, cannot be claimed

description: Channel split, deliberate: the graph channel rejects the record; the annotation channel warns on the line and falls back to the default 1.0. The two agree on the verdict and differ only in the remedy - a conformance test holds the scanner to core's verdict on generated values. Silent clamping was removed at conversion.
statement: A confidence is a real number between zero and one; out-of-range values are never silently repaired

description: Actor ids are audit attestations under repository access, not cryptographic identity proof. The default manifest ships an empty allowlist, which blocks every disposition (tracked in beads). Proven over the powerset of a two-actor universe crossed with the disposing actor and disposition presence.
statement: Only an actor listed in the repository manifest may dispose of a live proposal

description: Four conditions judged on loaded scope state by a pure function; write_disposition is load, judge, write under the lifecycle lock. Rejected and deferred decisions need no assertion. Proven over 108 points with a real artifact index, plus one example per refusal arm. Convergence with core's validate_disposition_links is recommended and tracked in beads. Amended 2026-08-10: an accepted disposition needs a prior assertion UNLESS its actor is human and it names a canonical artifact - a ratified tournament decision stands in for the swarm's assertion. Proven over 324 cases including the identity axis.
statement: A disposition is written only when its proposal exists and is undisposed, any named artifact exists in the scope, and an accepting decision follows an assertion or a human's ratified canonical artifact

description: The published page list is the authority, not the filesystem. Deliberately out of scope: bare anchors, absolute paths, any URL scheme, non-md destinations, trailing fragments, and images. Reference-style links are covered (pulldown-cmark resolves them to the same tag); image destinations are not seen. Parser-option asymmetry between check and serve is tracked in beads.
statement: A markdown link naming a local document must resolve to a page the docs site publishes

description: Records with no domain group as Unassigned rather than being dropped, so nothing vanishes from the wiki. Rule-to-requirement attribution is single-homed: one forward pass builds the inverse map both the domains page and the rule page read. Verified by property over generated requirement trees, including refines_into cycles.
statement: A requirement belongs to its own domain and every domain of its parents, and a rule to every domain of the requirements behind it

description: Twelve field sites (sources, requirements, resolutions, rules x origin thread/message; topics, questions x claimed by/at) are written once in visit_collaboration_fields; stripping and rejecting are two uses of the same walk, so the lists cannot drift. Proven per field site with coverage derived by running the real walk, plus a property that strip-then-validate always passes over all 4096 site subsets.
statement: A graph shared outside the repository carries no collaboration fields: export clears them and import rejects them through one shared field walk

description: One count predicate behind three flag families (resolution inputs, canonical artifact pair, source ref clause); refusal wording stays at each site. Proven exhaustively over count tuples against an oracle that derives the record count from the maximum rather than the first flag. The proposals handler's target pair now routes through the same predicate, and blank input content is refused by rule_resolution_input_content.
statement: A flag family naming part of a record must name all of it: required flags appear once per record, optional flags are omitted entirely or appear once per record

description: Differently-spelled git patterns are deliberately treated as different patterns; matching them would need pattern semantics and risk silently not ignoring the directory. Idempotence and byte-identical preservation of pre-existing lines are verified by property. Amended 2026-08-10: an unreadable .gitignore now propagates its error instead of being treated as empty and appended onto.
statement: A generated output directory gets exactly one ignore line, added if missing, never duplicated, whatever whitespace or line-ending style the existing file uses

description: The gap kinds: a requirement with no domain, no source refs, no resolving decision, or no produced rules; a rule missing either producer (owner ruling 2026-08-10: full tracing needs BOTH a producing requirement and a producing resolution; the gap names the missing end); a resolution resolving nothing; a source nothing references; a reference to a record that does not exist; an unresolved contradicts pair; an open question; an unexplored topic. Single seam consumed by the gaps command, prime, and the wiki assembler.
statement: compute_gaps decides what counts as an unfinished spot in a graph; a complete chain from source to rule with settled topics and questions yields no gaps

description: Enforced by construction: the predicate has one home in ids.rs and an invalid id is unrepresentable as a StableId or ScopeId (private fields, no bypassing impls, hand-written Deserialize routing through the constructor). All four shipped JSON-schema patterns agree with the runtime on a 50-value boundary corpus, verified by conformance against the emitted schemas. DispositionActor.id is deliberately outside the rule (actor identity, not a graph id).
statement: Every id in the graph is non-empty and uses only lowercase letters, digits, underscore, or hyphen

description: One classification (target state x identical/different x force) with three shells reading the filesystem in their own terms - file bytes, symlink target, directory tree. Proven over all 8 state x force calls against an independent oracle: nothing the install did not write is destroyed without force, and force changes nothing where the user has nothing at stake.
statement: Installing a skill never replaces something already at the target path unless force is passed; an identical install is a no-op

description: Nothing branches on the answer - it is the one line a reader takes as the account of the run, so it must never claim more or less than happened. Proven over the powerset of per-file outcome kinds, with order- and multiplicity-invariance checked rather than assumed.
statement: A skills install run is reported updated when any file changed, installed when files were only added, and unchanged otherwise

description: Anything the user touched is left alone: a single changed byte in the frontmatter or payload fails the hash and preserves the file. The version inside the header line is intentionally outside the hash, so a version bump alone does not orphan a file. The AGENTS.md marker block shares the proof core (hash_proves_ownership) but is a sibling decision without its own rule yet.
statement: A legacy skill file is deleted only when its embedded hash proves it is byte-for-byte what provenance installed

description: This gate is the admission half; the byte freeze is the SHA-256 fingerprint in core legacy_validation. Known bypass tracked in beads: the gate reads the proposal's current state, so a coordinated row-plus-flip write walks through - which is exactly how commit ac661a2 broke the frozen digests. The missing half is frozen-audit membership, and nothing refuses writes to the retired shard at write time. Amended 2026-08-10: admission now requires frozen-audit membership (the whole set must hash to the shipped disposition digest), closing the coordinated row-plus-state bypass; the left-proposed check remains as an honest superset.
statement: The retired promotion_decisions shard admits a row only when its proposal has already left proposed; it may hold only the shipped audit, never a new decision

description: Dot, dot-dot, empty segments, backslashes, and control characters are refused by name, so a hostile or buggy route cannot escape the staged output directory. classify_route is the single authority on acceptance and decomposition; the writer only maps its verdict to an error. Deliberate tightening at conversion: routes with empty segments were previously repaired silently and are now refused. Review note 2026-08-10: a drive-letter segment like C: is accepted as a plain name; harmless on the unix target the writer runs on, noted for any future Windows staging.
statement: A generated page is written only to a route bounded by slashes whose every segment is a plain name

description: Enforced by construction: GraphExport has no fields for proposals, assertions, dispositions, contributions, packets, or threads, and deny_unknown_fields refuses a returning document that names one. The rule marker sits on the struct because only the type governs both directions. The Value-typed escape hatches (expression/inputs/review_triggers) were deleted outright on 2026-08-10, closing the leak route.
statement: Only the canonical graph families travel in a pinned graph; collaboration and ideation records never enter the projection

description: A pinned graph names one scope; its digest and counts are read as facts about that scope alone, so a single stray record would smuggle another scope's data into a handover. The first offending record is named in the refusal. Proven per record family (11 families), with the family list tied to the GraphExport shape at compile time.
statement: Every record in a pinned graph must carry the scope id the graph claims, on export and import alike

description: Applied at both readings: the claim's own type and the evidence records behind it. Proven exhaustively over all six evidence types, with a second proof that the SpeculationMarker vocabulary names exactly the non-positive set in both directions. The evidence-side call is currently unreachable as a rejection path because the claim-side check fires first; it stays as the binding of the second reading.
statement: is_positive_evidence_type accepts every evidence type except unsupported and exploratory; speculation can never back an asserted claim

description: Those are outcomes of human decisions, not authorable claims. Proven exhaustively over all 28 state x link cases. Reachability differs by caller: the batch landing path and file validation hit it fully; the aggregate path guards it behind an already-proposed check for shipped-v1 tolerance; the CLI create path hard-codes legal values. The dead contradiction in proposal_from_input is tracked in beads.
statement: A modern proposal is written as proposed and nothing else, and may not carry its own duplicate-of or superseded-by verdict

description: The promotion_state column on a proposal row is a claim, not a verdict. A row that has already left proposed is frozen at what it claims; otherwise a human disposition decides (accepted, rejected, deferred); otherwise a recorded assertion makes the proposal asserted. Every proposal read applies this, so no caller sees a raw claim once lifecycle records exist. Proven exhaustively over all 56 classification cases.
statement: effective_proposal_state returns the disposition's verdict when a human disposed the proposal, asserted when evidence exists, and the row's claim otherwise

description: Whole-graph semantics: any cycle in the builds-on graph rejects the batch, and the error names the proposal where the walk closed, not the full path. Diamonds and shared ancestors are not cycles. Verified by property over generated DAGs with injected cycles against an independent reachability oracle.
statement: A proposal may not, through the assertions it builds on, end up building on itself

description: The undisposed precondition reads the projected state, not the row's stored claim. Reported reasons are never fabricated: every evidence path was both cited and touched, every territory reason equals the proposal's own target. The two live paths currently disagree on which triggers they can fire (tracked in beads).
statement: An undisposed proposal surfaces to a worker exactly when the work touches a file it cited or lands on the artifact it targets

name: Annotation vocabulary mirrors contract metadata
statement: External test annotations shall use the same metadata fields as Statesman contracts: name, description, tags (from Contract trait), rule code, coverage_level, confidence (from RuleContract). No new annotation-specific concepts.

name: No project management labels
statement: Annotations shall not include epic, feature, or story labels. Statesman is not a project management tool. The requirement tree provides hierarchy; Provenance derives structural context from the rule's graph chain.

name: Comment-based universal baseline
statement: A comment-based annotation format shall serve as the zero-dependency universal baseline that works in any programming language. Per-language native APIs (decorators, attributes, annotations) are optional ergonomic sugar that serialize to the same output format.

name: Simple key-value comment syntax
statement: Annotations shall use @statesman key: value syntax inside line comments. No function-call syntax, no parentheses, no quotes. Comments should look like comments, not code.

name: Rule field is the only required annotation
statement: The @statesman rule: field shall be the only required annotation field. All other fields (name, description, tags, coverage, confidence, intent) are optional with sensible defaults: name inferred from function, coverage defaults to full, confidence defaults to 1.0.

name: Function-scoped by default with file-level override
statement: Annotations immediately above a test function shall apply to that test only (function-scoped). Annotations at the top of a file before any function shall apply to all tests in that file (file-scoped). Function-level annotations override file-level for the same field.

name: Multi-rule via separate rule lines
statement: A single test may cover multiple rules using one @statesman rule: line per rule. Coverage and confidence following a rule line apply to that rule. Coverage and confidence preceding all rules or standing alone apply to all rules in the block.

name: Comment prefix detected from file extension
statement: The scanner shall detect the line comment prefix from file extension: // for Rust/C/Java/Go/JS/TS/C#/Swift/Kotlin, # for Python/Ruby/Shell/YAML/TOML, -- for SQL/Lua/Haskell, % for Erlang/LaTeX. Block comments are not supported in v1.

name: Line-oriented parser only
statement: The scanner shall be a line-oriented text parser with comment-prefix awareness. It shall not parse ASTs, resolve imports, execute tests, or modify source code.

name: Human-attributable writes
statement: All writes to provenance artifacts must be attributable to a human identity (seat owner). AI-authored content shall be marked via message role=assistant while retaining the owning human as the author.

name: WorkOS role and permissions in JWT claims
statement: The control plane must extract role and permissions from WorkOS access tokens and include them in Statesman JWT ClaimsProperties so downstream services (Provenance, broker) can read them without additional API calls.

name: Per-mutation permission enforcement in Provenance
statement: Every Provenance mutation must call requirePermission() with the appropriate resource:action permission string. The check must be backward-compatible: coarse read/write scopes grant all reads or all writes respectively, and admin grants everything.

name: Agent tokens use sm_agent_ prefix and carry identity_type
statement: Agent tokens must use the sm_agent_ prefix to distinguish them from human API keys (sm_live_). When exchanged for a JWT, the claims must include identity_type=agent, agent_id, and owner_id fields.

name: Agent tokens must have mandatory expiration
statement: Agent tokens must have a non-null expires_at timestamp. The system must provide a token rotation command. Expired tokens must be rejected at exchange time.

name: Agent tokens inherit project scope from owner by default
statement: When agent_tokens.project_ids is NULL, the agent inherits its owner's project access. Explicit project_ids must be a subset of the owner's access.

name: Default roles exclude resolutions:approve for agents
statement: The system default role sets (read-only, contributor, analyst) must not include the resolutions:approve permission. Only full-access and custom organization roles may grant approval rights.

name: Delegation tokens must narrow permissions, never widen
statement: When an agent creates a delegation token for another agent, the delegated permissions must be a strict subset of the delegating agent's permissions. The human owner remains the same. The delegation chain must be traceable via created_by_agent_id.

name: Agents attributed via synthetic Convex user records
statement: Agents must have synthetic user records in the Convex users table with isAgent=true and ownerUserId linking to the human owner. This preserves all existing createdBy queries and UI rendering while enabling agent-aware display.

name: CLI agent output uses HAL+JSON with navigable _links
statement: All Provenance CLI commands that output JSON shall include HAL-style _links on each artifact, providing commands for available operations (self, traceability, graph, related artifacts). Agents consuming CLI output shall be able to discover and follow graph relationships without prior knowledge of available commands. Raw Convex JSON without _links shall be available via --raw-json for debugging.

name: Top-level coverage commands
statement: Coverage commands shall live at 'statesman coverage', not nested under 'statesman provenance'. Coverage spans both contract coverage from the broker and external test evidence from annotations.

name: Thread diffs on definitive changes only
statement: When coverage changes are pushed from a scan (not a dry-run), diffs shall be posted to affected rule threads in Provenance: new coverage added, coverage removed, confidence or level changed. Dry-runs shall not post to threads.

name: External coverage stored in broker
statement: External test coverage evidence shall be stored in the broker via RuleContract with mapping_source=imported. The broker is the single source of truth for all coverage data. Provenance pulls coverage from the broker unchanged.

name: Runtime fields optional on coverage API
statement: The broker coverage API and annotation format shall not require runtime fields (pass/fail result, timestamp, duration, pass rate). These fields must be optional extensions that future runtime reporters can provide without breaking the static-analysis-only path.

name: External test evidence as first-class records
statement: External tests shall be stored as evidence records in the broker containing test metadata (file, line, function, name, description, tags). RuleContract shall link to evidence records the same way it links to contract versions. No nullable FKs.

name: Bulk evidence import endpoint
statement: The broker shall expose a bulk import endpoint for external test evidence that accepts the scanner's JSON output and creates/updates evidence records and rule linkages in a single request. One-at-a-time creation via existing link_contract is insufficient for CI pipelines scanning hundreds of tests.

name: Four coverage subcommands
statement: The statesman coverage command shall have four subcommands: 'scan' (scan + push in one shot), 'scan --dry-run' (scan only, output JSON, do not push or post threads), 'report' (accept pre-computed scan JSON from stdin and push to broker), and 'status' (show current coverage summary from broker).

name: Normalized artifact storage
statement: All provenance artifacts (sources, requirements, resolutions, rules) shall be stored in separate normalized tables with typed graph edges, not embedded sub-documents

name: Recursive requirement hierarchy
statement: Requirements shall compose recursively via parentId to arbitrary depth without artificial tier limits. No separate initiative/epic/story types.

description: The function validate_edge_endpoint is the rule. Its branches: a references edge is accepted only from a source to a requirement; a refines_into, depends_on, contradicts, or supersedes edge only between requirements; a needs edge only from a requirement to a resolution; resolves and spawns edges only from a resolution to a requirement; a produces edge only from a requirement or resolution to a rule. Any triple not matched by a branch is rejected, so no edge may leave a rule and only a produces edge may end at one.
statement: Every edge triple is checked against the endpoint table and rejected with InvalidEdgeEndpoint when its endpoints do not match its type's row

name: Bounded artifact-attached ideation threads
statement: Each multi-persona ideation run shall target exactly one primary Provenance artifact or problem and shall record bounded participant comments plus a synthesis in an artifact-attached thread.

name: Persona profile attribution
statement: Every persona participant output shall record the persona/profile name, profile version, prompt/template version, executing agent identity, model/config metadata, timestamp, target artifact, and owning human or service attribution.

name: Human promotion gate for ideation outputs
statement: Persona-generated ideation comments, synthesis, and proposal cards shall not become canonical requirements, resolutions, rules, or work items unless a human explicitly accepts or edits the proposal, with the promoted artifact linked back to the originating thread messages and run metadata.

name: Idempotent ideation job writes
statement: Ideation job writes shall use deterministic idempotency keys for participant comments, synthesis, proposal extraction, and artifact links so retries or duplicate workers do not create duplicate Provenance records.

name: Visible partial ideation failures
statement: If any persona participant, model call, synthesis step, or thread post fails, the ideation run shall expose partial status, failed step identity, retry state, and diagnostic context rather than presenting the run as fully successful.

name: Dissent and evidence preservation
statement: Ideation synthesis shall explicitly preserve consensus, contested claims, minority objections, evidence strength, unsupported speculation, source gaps, and open assumptions; it shall not collapse disagreement into unqualified consensus.

name: Stable ideation run correlation ID
statement: Every ideation run SHALL mint a stable ideation_run_id that is recorded on the work item, participant executions, thread comments, synthesis, proposal cards, retries, failures, and any promoted artifacts.

name: Ideation run status lifecycle
statement: Ideation runs SHALL expose an explicit status lifecycle: queued, running, synthesizing, succeeded, partial, failed_retryable, failed_terminal, and cancelled. A run with any failed participant or failed post SHALL NOT be reported as succeeded.

name: Ideation input snapshot
statement: Each ideation run SHALL record an input snapshot containing target artifact type/id, selected source IDs, graph scope/hash or timestamp, existing thread IDs considered, persona profile versions, prompt/template versions, model identifiers, and configured budget limits.

name: Bounded participant and round limits
statement: An ideation run SHALL enforce configured maximums for participant count, rounds, model calls, tokens, wall-clock duration, and generated bytes before execution starts; exceeding any limit SHALL cancel or partially fail the run visibly.

name: Machine-readable run inspection
statement: The system SHALL provide a machine-readable inspection view for an ideation run that returns run status, target artifact, input snapshot, participant statuses, message IDs, synthesis ID, proposal IDs, retry attempts, failure diagnostics, and promotion decisions.

name: Deterministic participant slots
statement: Each participant output SHALL be keyed by (ideation_run_id, round_number, participant_slot, persona_profile_version). Retrying the same slot SHALL update or reuse the same logical output and SHALL NOT create an additional participant comment.

name: Participant contribution schema
statement: Each persona participant comment SHALL include structured sections for stance, strongest finding, evidence references, risks, objections, suggested artifact changes, uncertainty, and open questions.

name: Evidence labels on participant claims
statement: Participant comments SHALL label each material claim as source-backed, graph-backed, code-backed, prior-thread-backed, inference, or speculation. Speculative claims SHALL NOT be presented as findings in synthesis without the speculation label.

name: Challenge comments reference specific claims
statement: When a persona challenges another persona, the challenge SHALL reference the specific participant comment, claim, or proposal being challenged and SHALL state the reason for disagreement; generic dissent without a target is invalid.

name: No unsupported authoritative persona claims
statement: Persona participants SHALL NOT state unsupported recommendations as authoritative product truth. If a participant recommends action without source or graph support, the output SHALL explicitly mark the recommendation as unsupported or exploratory.

name: Synthesis packet required sections
statement: Each ideation synthesis SHALL include sections for summary, consensus, contested claims, minority objections, evidence gaps, unsupported speculation, open questions, suggested artifacts, and required human decisions.

name: Typed ideation proposal cards
statement: Ideation synthesis SHALL emit proposal cards typed as one of: requirement_candidate, resolution_candidate, rule_candidate, work_item_candidate, source_gap, question, or no_action. Each proposal card SHALL declare exactly one type.

name: Proposal card traceability fields
statement: Each proposal card SHALL record origin participant message IDs, supporting claim IDs or excerpts, evidence level, dissent status, confidence, target artifact if applicable, proposed text, and promotion state.

name: Proposal promotion state lifecycle
statement: Proposal cards SHALL expose a promotion state lifecycle: proposed, accepted, rejected, deferred, duplicate, superseded. Only accepted proposals MAY create or update canonical Provenance artifacts.

name: Duplicate proposal detection
statement: Before presenting proposal cards, the synthesis step SHALL detect duplicates within the same run by comparing proposal type, normalized proposed text, target artifact, and source evidence; duplicates SHALL be merged or marked duplicate.

name: Promoted artifact backlink requirement
statement: When a proposal card is accepted and promoted, the created or updated artifact SHALL link back to the ideation_run_id, synthesis message, origin participant comments, accepted proposal card, and human approval event.

name: Outcome-first ideation thread layout
statement: The default thread presentation for an ideation run SHALL show synthesis, proposal cards, contested claims, open questions, and visible failures before raw participant transcript content.

name: Raw transcript retained but collapsed
statement: Raw persona outputs and model transcripts SHALL be retained for audit when available, but SHALL be collapsed or secondary in the default UI so users are not required to read full transcripts to identify outcomes.

name: Persona label distinct from executor identity
statement: Ideation UI and API output SHALL display persona/profile labels separately from authenticated executor identity and owner attribution, so readers can distinguish the simulated perspective from the agent or human account that performed the write.

name: Synthesis readability budget
statement: Ideation synthesis SHALL be concise enough to serve as a review brief: it SHALL include no more than seven top-level findings unless explicitly expanded, and each proposal card SHALL be independently scannable without reading the transcript.

name: Ideation project and target scope isolation
statement: An ideation run SHALL only read and write artifacts within the target artifact's project and configured scope. It SHALL reject participant prompts, tool calls, or proposal promotions that target artifacts outside the authorized project/scope.

name: Source access and redaction enforcement
statement: Ideation runs SHALL respect source access policy and redaction rules. If a participant lacks access to a source, the run SHALL omit that source from the participant input snapshot and SHALL NOT leak its contents in comments or synthesis.

name: Ideation cancellation and deadline handling
statement: Ideation runs SHALL support cancellation and hard deadlines. A cancelled or deadline-expired run SHALL stop scheduling new participant work, preserve completed outputs, mark unfinished participant slots as cancelled or timed_out, and post or expose partial status.

name: Ideation rate and budget limits
statement: The system SHALL enforce per-project and per-run limits for concurrent ideation runs, participant count, token spend, model call count, and thread writes. Limit exhaustion SHALL produce a visible bounded failure rather than silently skipping participants.

name: Unsafe ideation output handling
statement: If participant output is unsafe, policy-violating, or unsuitable for thread posting, the run SHALL record a sanitized failure marker with participant slot, reason category, and retry state; unsafe content SHALL NOT be posted as normal artifact discussion.

name: One active ideation thread per parent under concurrency
statement: Concurrent ideation posting for the same parent artifact SHALL result in exactly one active thread for that parent. The implementation SHALL prevent or reconcile duplicate active threads created by concurrent find-or-create operations.

name: Concurrent participant posting acceptance test
statement: A validation test SHALL run at least five participant posts concurrently against one target artifact and assert that the result contains one active thread, exactly one participant comment per participant slot, one synthesis record, and no duplicate threads or comments.

name: Participant retry idempotency acceptance test
statement: A validation test SHALL simulate a participant post succeeding followed by a worker crash before completion marking, then retry the same participant slot and assert that no duplicate comment or proposal is created and the existing output is associated with the retry attempt.

name: Partial failure acceptance test
statement: A validation test SHALL force one participant failure and assert that the ideation run status is partial or failed_retryable, successful participant outputs remain visible, failed slot diagnostics are inspectable, and synthesis does not claim a complete panel.

name: Human promotion traceability acceptance test
statement: A validation test SHALL accept a proposal card into a canonical artifact and assert that the artifact links to the ideation run, proposal card, synthesis, supporting participant comments, source evidence, and human approval event.

name: Run inspection conformance acceptance test
statement: A validation test SHALL call the ideation run inspection surface after success, partial failure, and cancellation and assert that all required fields from PROV-IDEATE-011 are present and internally consistent.

name: Ideation output schema validation
statement: Before an ideation run is marked succeeded, the implementation SHALL validate participant comments, synthesis, and proposal cards against the required schemas; missing required sections or malformed proposal cards SHALL produce partial or failed_retryable status.

name: Scanner lives in Statesman CLI
statement: The static analysis scanner shall be built into the Statesman CLI binary, not as a standalone tool. This gives external tests access to traceability, impact analysis, gap detection, audit trails, and CI integration for free.

name: Scan-time stale annotation validation
statement: The scanner shall cross-reference extracted annotations against the project's active rules and warn on unknown rule codes, deprecated rules, and archived rules to prevent false coverage confidence.

name: Tree-sitter AST-based scanning
statement: The scanner shall use tree-sitter for AST parsing with statically linked grammars. Comment-to-code association, function detection, and block boundaries shall be derived from the AST, not line-oriented regex heuristics. This supersedes PROV-ANNOT-015.

name: JSON scanner output format
statement: The scanner shall produce JSON output containing: project_id, scanned_at timestamp, files_scanned count, tests_found count, an annotations array (file, line, function, name, description, tags, rules with code/coverage/confidence), and a warnings array for stale or unknown annotations.

name: Full scan every run in v1
statement: The scanner shall perform a full scan of all matching files on every invocation in v1. Incremental scanning (content hashing, git-based change detection) is a future optimization, not a v1 requirement.

name: One-directional broker sync
statement: Rule definitions shall sync one-directionally from Provenance to the Statesman broker. The broker owns contract-to-rule linkage and coverage tracking. Provenance shall not consume broker state.

name: Bidirectional traceability
statement: The system shall support both forward traceability (source -> requirements -> resolutions -> rules) and backward traceability (rule -> resolution -> requirement -> source) as first-class query operations

name: ELK layout with zone partitioning
statement: The canvas UI shall use ELK for automatic graph layout with zone partitioning that groups nodes by artifact type into distinct visual regions

description: Crash residue is reported for operator choice, never silently adopted or deleted - proven over all 128 output-kind x artifact-residue states with the output and residue asserted byte-for-byte untouched after every refusal (unix; Windows keeps the reparse-point example). The five artifact names are minted once in ArtifactLeaves. Amended 2026-08-10: a refusal now names every residue artifact present in role order, and an unsafe lock is a fact about a listed path rather than an early refusal hiding the rest.
statement: Publishing refuses to start when the output is not a real directory or when leftover artifacts from an interrupted run are present

description: The decision is seven facts evaluated in one function: the must path (a qualified proposal cannot be left unasserted) reads all seven from records; the may path (an assertion is allowed) passes three as witnessed by the assertion record itself. Proven over all 128 fact assignments, with every refusal blaming a genuinely unmet fact. Replaced a drifted inline copy in swarm-backtrace preflight that rejected runs the store would accept.
statement: A synthesis packet qualifies a proposal for assertion only when it owns the proposal's target, adjudicates that proposal and no other, and the proposal's cited claims stand uncontested with no blocking gap and no pending human decision

description: The choke point where a stored line becomes a record guards every family - a hand-edited version-2 row fails list, check, and export instead of loading silently. A line with no schema_version makes no claim and is left to its own deserializer; cross-scope edges are filtered before the guard so another scope's future data stays ignored rather than fatal. Known residual: StateStore::manifest() is still unguarded (tracked in beads). Amended 2026-08-10: the write path bypassed this guard - jsonl::mutate_jsonl_locked read shards with plain serde and no version check, so a create beside a hand-edited version-2 row re-serialised it from the fields the current struct recognised and dropped the rest, laundering into the supported layout the record every reader refuses. That read now calls the same guard on the same raw JSON before any mutation, so a refusal leaves the shard byte-identical; the exhaustion proof runs all three loaders. Remaining unguarded readers of stored content, all non-lossy Value round-trips: merge's reader, the import scope-writer's edge re-read, and StateStore::manifest().
statement: A stored record claiming an unsupported schema version is refused before it becomes a record, on the read path and on the read every write is built on, naming the file, line, record, and both versions

description: Absence counts as a value a side can hold: identical changes are kept once, a delete against an untouched record wins silently, and a delete against an edit keeps the surviving side and reports delete_modify. Add/add with different content reports its own add_add kind, and conflicts carry the base pre-image. Proven exhaustively over all 14 reachable (base, ours, theirs) cases. Amended 2026-08-10: the driver is wired via .gitattributes, a conflicted merge exits non-zero so git falls back to conflict, and merged edge shards are validated against the endpoint table before writing - the merge no longer launders records past the write gate.
statement: merge_records keeps the moved side when only one side of a merge moved a record, and keeps ours and reports the clash when both moved differently

description: One comparison - resolved candidate equals container/name - rejects dot-dot traversal and symlinks at once, and callers may only act on the returned resolved path. An already-gone mode skips the leaf probe when nothing remains on disk. Tightened at conversion: a leaf symlink at a sibling inside the transactions directory was previously accepted. create_real_directory is the ancestor half (the cache itself is real), cross-referenced, not folded. Amended 2026-08-10: the touched leaf must also be a real directory - a regular file named by a marker is refused up front rather than failing inside removal.
statement: Recovery touches a directory only when it resolves to a real direct child of the repository cache's transactions directory

description: Gates all three read verbs; a refused reference fails every verb identically and names the mismatched field. Every mismatch arm has a direct test; exhaustion is deliberately not claimed because the input is unbounded git state. Known gap tracked in beads: exact-export documents are not self-verifying.
statement: A graph reference is honoured only if its commit exists here, the repository identity matches, the graph at that commit hashes to the recorded digest, and the id is the hash of exactly those parts

description: Version 1; grf1_/git1_ identities of exactly 64 lowercase hex; the fixed .provenance/state store path; a scope id ScopeId accepts; a full 40- or 64-character lowercase commit id, never an abbreviation; a sha256: digest; a correlation with both parts filled if present. A JSON Schema replica exists in the cli schema handler; a conformance test pushes 59 boundary values through both and asserts agreeing verdicts. One known divergence (schema_version 1.0) is tracked in beads.
statement: GraphReference::validate refuses any reference whose fields deviate from the issued shape

description: The badge must not let resolved lie: plain Resolved appears exactly when a decision or rule stands behind the requirement, and the admission appears exactly when none does. Non-resolved statuses never gain the suffix. Proven over every status with the count axes bucketed to zero, one, and many.
statement: A resolved requirement with no decisions and no rules is labelled Resolved (no decisions or rules), never plain Resolved

description: Blank means empty or whitespace; refused, never repaired. Enforced at deserialization via a wire-shape TryFrom, so the CLI create path and import share one gate. The reference is deliberately not resolved against the graph - it may cite legislation, a file, or a conversation the graph will never see; the rule decides something was named, not that it exists.
statement: A resolution input's reference and summary must not be blank; a field that names nothing locates nothing

description: A later version means a different layout that today's structs would half-read silently. One function guards the five core sites with byte-identical messages; the store's four sibling copies and the unguarded non-ideation read path are tracked in beads. Proven exhaustively over five kinds x versions 0, 1, 2, and u32 max.
statement: Ideation records are read only at schema version one

description: A source pin locates; a reference commit identifies. The strict shape (exactly 40 or 64 lowercase) deliberately lives in rule_reference_wellformed - two rules sharing the word commit, split on purpose, not drift. Verified by property against a written-out character-set oracle.
statement: A source commit pin is 7 to 64 hexadecimal characters, any case

description: The write-time enforcement of rule_prov_ideate_032's exactly-one-active-thread invariant, by reconciliation rather than refusal: resolved and archived threads and other records are untouched, and the publication lock serializes concurrent posts so the race cannot happen. Verified by property through the real write path. Known gap tracked in beads: import writes threads wholesale with no thread validation.
statement: When a write picks a record's canonical thread, the same write archives every other active thread of that record

name: Search, domains, traceability order
statement: At 1440x900 and 390x844, the homepage search control must precede every repeated domain row, and the traceability call to action must follow the domain section.
source_section: Human disposition of Directions A-C; candidate constraints 1-3 and 8

name: Plain homepage language
statement: Reader-facing homepage copy must use everyday labels for the project, documentation, records, and missing evidence; it must not use the word 'corpus'.

name: Honest homepage search coverage
statement: Until offline search indexes resolutions and sources, homepage search copy must state that it covers requirements and rules.

name: Exact compact traceability summary
statement: The homepage must show one exact traceability finding count linked to its complete findings route and must render no individual gap cards.
source_section: Candidate constraint 4; human graft from Direction C

description: Replacing a directory destroys everything in it. A marker that exists but does not prove ownership (foreign generator, unsupported version, oversized, malformed, or not a regular file) is always a refusal, never a licence to overwrite, whichever policy asked. Proven exhaustively over all 28 policy x marker x emptiness cases.
statement: The wiki replaces a directory only when its marker proves this generator published it, when the directory is empty, or when it is the generator-owned default output

description: The known hosts are GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket; with no remote or a self-hosted one, code references stay plain text because a repo-relative link would 404 against the wiki's own routes. Verified by property over generated references crossed with remote states, and by exhaustion over the host x line-anchor table. Amended 2026-08-10: a bare dotted token with no directory and no line group is prose, never a file path - payroll.rs alone stays plain text; src/payroll.rs or payroll.rs:12 links. One predicate governs whole-field references and free-text spans alike.
statement: A reference renders as a link only when the link would work: a web address as it stands, or a file path a known code host can turn into a real address; everything else stays plain text
